messages:
maria nguyen: Proposal — add an ingestion-level attribute scrubber that hashes prompts and salts user IDs before they hit our observability exporters. Posting a short sketch, want quick feedback before I draft an RFC.

chris ford: +1 on doing this at ingest. Q: do we salt per-org? If yes we lose cross-org dedupe for abuse detection.

maria nguyen: I'm leaning per-org salt to avoid leaking cross-customer correlations. We can still detect anomalous volumes via count metrics (not raw ids). Salt stored in KMS, rotate monthly.

samir patel: Also: hashed prompt values are still high-cardinality if we keep full 64-hex SHA. Two suggestions: truncate to 8 chars to reduce cardinality (accept collisions) and add a prompt_length_bucket attribute (e.g., <50, 50-200, >200) to help dashboards.

kenji watanabe: Strongly agree: never store raw prompts in telemetry. For debugging/evals we have opt-in pipeline (separate secure store). For general telemetry we only keep prompt_hash and length_bucket + a sample_id. Also enforce per-hash rate limits so one prompt can't blow up cardinality.

chris ford: For exporters: we need to scrub before exporting to third parties (Datadog, Honeycomb). Internally, ES cluster can keep more detail but we should have retention rules: full attributes for 90 days, then roll up to aggregates for 365d.

maria nguyen: Drafting config idea (pseudo-OTel pipeline):
```
processors:
  attribute_scrubber:
    rules:
      - key: prompt
        action: hash
        algo: sha256
        truncate: 8
      - key: user_id
        action: salt_hash
        salt_source: org_salt_kms
      - key: session_id
        action: drop
exports:
  internal_es: {...}
  third_party: { scrubbed: true }
```

samir patel: Nice. Two more operational things: 1) tail/adaptive sampling so we keep full attributes for traces that hit error/latency thresholds (e.g., >95p latency or non-2xx). 2) a per-tenant cardinality quota that rejects/normalizes extra unique attribute values once limit reached.

kenji watanabe: On sampling: we should implement deterministic sampling for low-volume tenants so dashboards are stable. For adaptive tail sampling, mark kept traces with a `telemetry_policy=full` tag.

chris ford: One security note: hashed prompt + sample_id could still be reidentified if someone has the original prompt list. Make sure salts are secret and rotate. Also treat prompt_hash as an internal identifier — don't export to customers.

maria nguyen: Good points. For rollout UX: console should show "top prompt_hashes" with sample counts and a "view sample" button that only works for opt-in eval datasets. Don't expose raw text in normal dashboards.

ops-bot: Deploy window scheduled: telemetry-ingest-v2 -> canary starts 03/19 02:00 UTC, full 03/19 08:00 UTC.

maria nguyen: OK I'll incorporate feedback: per-org salt, truncate prompt hash to 8, length buckets, per-hash rate limits, adaptive tail sampling + deterministic baseline. I'll open RFC and include a small perf test to measure extra CPU on ingest.

ingest-bot: Note: we should add a metric for "attributes_scrubbed_per_minute" to track scrubber load.

chris ford: One last: update docs + SDKs so library-level instrumentation can opt into sending `prompt_raw` only to the opt-in endpoint.

maria nguyen: Thanks all — RFC incoming later today. :Thanks:
